job_title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Monetization)
job_description:
In 2026, we launched Computer, the defining product for the new era of agentic AI. Millions of people now use Perplexity to transform knowledge into action, and every action an agent takes is metered, budgeted, and settled through the billing platform this role owns.

As a monetization engineer at Perplexity, you'll own the abstractions that let product teams ship new SKUs, run pricing experiments, and convert users into paying customers, without needing to understand billing internals. The usage-based billing system this team owns is foundational to Perplexity Computer and our agentic products: metering every agent action in real time, enforcing credit budgets, and settling costs across entirely new interaction models. You'll work across subscriptions, usage-based billing, and enterprise contracts to ensure every revenue path is reliable, observable, and easy to extend.

Tech Stack: Python | Go | Stripe | PostgreSQL | AWS | Docker




WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT

 - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both the AI native and AI curious.

 - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

 - Entrepreneurship. We think like founders, act with urgency, and hustle to deliver for each other and our users.

 - Scholarship. Work among highly talented peers, pursuing knowledge and truth, upleveling ourselves, our teams, and our products.

 - Partnership. We amplify each others' strengths, break down silos, and give selflessly to help our colleagues deliver excellence.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design, build, and own the billing platform and monetization systems that power Computer and every paid experience across Perplexity.

 - Lead features end-to-end, from problem definition through technical design, implementation, and launch, including the billing API abstractions that let product teams ship new SKUs, pricing models, and monetization experiments with minimal friction.

 - Build and operate the subscription, invoicing, and usage-based billing systems that serve millions of users across consumer and enterprise plans.

 - Hill-climb on reliability: tiered SLOs organized by customer impact, proactive monitoring, and alerting to catch revenue-affecting issues before customers do.

 - Partner closely with Finance, Data Science, Growth, Security, Support, and go-to-market teams to keep billing data accurate, auditable, and compliant, and to expand payment method coverage and optimize authorization rates globally.

 - Build internal tooling that empowers Support and Finance to diagnose and resolve billing issues quickly.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of professional software engineering experience.

 - Direct experience building or scaling billing, payments, subscription, or monetization systems.

 - Deep familiarity with payment processors (Stripe, Square, etc.), including subscriptions, invoicing, disputes, refunds, and webhooks.

 - Demonstrated experience and appetite for building in-house billing solutions that rival leading best-in-class buy options.

 - Strong backend engineering skills in Python with the ability to reason about complex distributed systems.

 - Experience with relational databases (PostgreSQL) and making data-informed decisions to prioritize work.

 - Strong product judgment, you translate user and stakeholder problems into simple, effective technical solutions.

 - Self-motivated with strong ownership instincts, you ship major features ahead of schedule and drive improvements without asking for permission.

 - Track record of cross-functional collaboration with Finance, Support, or Growth stakeholders.

 - Genuine interest and adoption of AI products and willingness to learn quickly.


NICE TO HAVE

 - 2+ years of hands-on experience with the Stripe APIs and SDKs.

 - Experience with usage-based or metered billing models, especially metering agent actions, tokens, or other non-traditional units.

 - Experience with Apple and Google Play in-app purchase billing.

 - Familiarity with growth experimentation and PLG/self-serve SaaS monetization.

 - Experience building platform constructs that support pricing experiments and A/B testing.

 - Full-stack experience (our frontend is Next.js/React/TypeScript).

 - Experience in a regulatory or compliance-heavy billing environment.

 - Time spent at a fast-growing startup or on a high-ownership engineering team.

We're looking for a Growth Brand Designer to sit at the intersection of brand craft and growth performance. You'll be the designer who makes Perplexity's highest-volume, highest-leverage marketing surfaces — paid ads, social, lifecycle email, and campaign assets — look unmistakably Perplexity while actually moving the numbers.

This is a shipping role, but it's equally a thinking role. Strategic concepting is a big part of the job: you'll sit with the Growth team as an ideator — generating campaign concepts, testing hypotheses, and shaping the creative strategy behind the work — not just executing briefs handed to you. The ideas you bring to the table matter as much as the assets you ship.

You'll produce a steady stream of ad and campaign creative across formats and channels, then work with Growth to read the results and iterate. You care about conversion and craft in equal measure: you'd never ship an off-brand asset to win a test, and you'd never hide behind polish when the data says a concept isn't working.

You'll report into the Brand/Creative Studio team and work closely with Growth, Product Marketing, Brand, and our motion and web designers.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Drive strategic concepting for growth campaigns — bring original ideas, angles, and creative territories to the table, and shape the brief rather than just receiving it

 - Operate as a true ideation partner to the Growth team: co-develop campaign strategy, propose test hypotheses, and pitch concepts that open up new creative directions

 - Own the design of growth creative end-to-end — paid social and display ads, campaign assets, and lifecycle email — from concept to shipped asset

 - Design for volume and velocity: build variant sets, test hypotheses, and iterate on winners with the Growth team using real performance data

 - Turn product launches and GTM campaigns into ad creative that lands on every channel it runs — static, animated, and everything in between

 - Build and maintain scalable ad and email templates so high-frequency asset production stays fast and on-brand

 - Partner with Brand to keep visual consistency across every growth touchpoint as our brand system evolves

 - Collaborate with our motion designer and web designer so campaigns feel cohesive from the first ad impression to the landing page

 - Bring a strong point of view on what makes performance creative great — and push back when a "best practice" would cheapen the brand


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - A strong portfolio of growth and brand design work — paid ads, social campaigns, lifecycle email, campaign systems — that shows both craft and results

 - Proven strategic concepting ability: you can show campaigns where the idea was yours, not just the execution, and articulate the thinking behind them

 - Excellent visual design skills with a clear sense of brand, typography, layout, and composition

 - Hands-on experience designing performance creative at a consumer or prosumer tech company, including working directly with growth or performance marketing teams

 - Fluency reading creative performance data (CTR, conversion, hook rates) and translating it into design decisions

 - Ability to work fast, manage a high volume of deliverables across channels, and iterate quickly without dropping the quality bar

 - Fluency in Figma and the Adobe Creative Suite

 - An instinct for building repeatable systems — templates, variant frameworks, asset kits — rather than one-off files

 - 5+ years of industry experience


NICE TO HAVE

 - Motion design skills — animated ads, short-form video for social, or After Effects fluency

 - Familiarity with ad platform specs and constraints (Meta, Google, TikTok, X, YouTube) and how they shape creative decisions

 - Experience using AI-assisted design and image-generation workflows to scale creative output

 - Copywriting instincts — you can tighten a headline when there's no writer in the room

job_title: Member of Technical Staff, (Software Engineer, Experience)
job_description:
The charter of Perplexity’s Core Experience team is to create a cohesive, intuitive, and delightful user experience by integrating cutting-edge AI capabilities and research into a unified system. The Core Experience team works closely with product design teams to ship a world-class web app that’s used by millions of people every day. We imagine and build the interfaces through which people experience the promise of AI.




We are seeking a talented engineer with an uncompromising dedication to the craft of frontend web development. You’ll help us to define the future of human-agent collaboration: establishing intuitive mental-models, patterns, and state-representation. You’ll work closely with design to prototype, architect, and engineer novel interfaces for interacting with AI collaborators.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build and ship polished, high-craft, intuitive web interfaces

 - Constantly improve high-visibility surfaces like agent chat threads, artifact editing, and message composition

 - Partner directly with design to turn visionary ideas into production implementations

 - Solve complex problems across architecture, state-management, animation, and performance-optimization

 - Collaborate with capabilities and research teams to synthesize the latest research into coherent production experiences

 - Support other product teams by designing reusable libraries and SDKs to maintain a high quality-bar across all surfaces of the product


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong proficiency in modern web technologies: React, TypeScript, CSS, etc.

 - Exceptional taste: relentless attention to detail, from aesthetics to performance to code-quality

 - Comfortable owning projects end-to-end, working at high velocity in an ambiguous environment where the industry changes by the day

 - Keen product sensibilities: being able to reason about what will work, what won’t, and articulate why

 - Customer obsession: always thinking about how what you’re building will touch the person on the other side of the screen

Perplexity is looking for a Content Designer to shape the words across our products. You'll design the language people see and hear across our family of Perplexity apps, from the first screen of onboarding to the way an agent explains what it's doing. Fundamentally, we are all writers. Our product is primarily spoken language and written product; but as we scale, we want someone who will continue to work on clarity, usefulness, and keep it unmistakably Perplexity.



You're a designer first? You're an engineer first? You're a writer first? Your shape is not conventional, and you wear many hats. You are fluent in AI tooling. You have strong UX fundamentals and good product instincts. You use language to solve product problems: flows, naming, information architecture, error states, permissions, and moments where people need to trust what the product is telling them. You command words. You command agents, and make decisions about words. You can write one perfect line, and you can build the system that keeps thousands of lines consistent.



You'll sit on the Design Systems team and work closely with product designers, engineers, PMs, research, brand, and marketing. (Again) You're fluent in AI-powered tools and use it every day. You understand how models behave, how prompts and system instructions shape what people see, and how to define and judge quality when the output isn't fully deterministic.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and write in-product language across web, mobile, desktop, and voice, including UI copy, flows, onboarding, notifications, empty states, errors, and in-product education

 - Partner with product designers from the start of a project, shaping flows, structure, and information architecture as well as the words in them

 - Name features and products, and own terminology, navigation labels, and taxonomies so the product stays easy to understand as it grows

 - Make complex AI and agent behavior understandable, including what the product is doing, why, what it can't do, and when it needs a person's input

 - Shape how AI-generated content reads by writing and refining prompts and system instructions, and help define voice and response style for our models in product

 - Define content quality standards and help build evaluation criteria, datasets, and reviewer guidance for AI-generated content

 - Build and maintain voice and tone guidelines, content patterns, and content guidance in our design system so every team can write well

 - Use research, data, and experiments to test language and improve comprehension, activation, and task completion

 - Partner with brand and marketing so product language and our external voice feel like one company

 - Work with internationalization partners so the product reads well in every language we support

 - Review copy in code and ship small language changes directly when it's the fastest path


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of experience in content design, UX writing, or product design, shipping software at scale

 - An excellent portfolio that shows how your language shaped product decisions, with clear before and after examples and your role in each

 - Strong UX fundamentals, including interaction design, information architecture, usability, and accessibility

 - Good product sensibility and judgment about what to build, what to cut, and what matters most to people

 - Exceptional writing and editing skills, with range from precise interface copy to clear explanations and confident naming

 - Strong AI fluency, including hands-on experience writing prompts, working with LLMs, and judging the quality of AI-generated content

 - Systems thinking, with experience building content frameworks, style guides, or terminology that scale across teams

 - Clear communication, with the ability to explain content decisions and tradeoffs to designers, engineers, and leaders

 - You care about shipping great software more than anything else


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience designing content for AI products, assistants, agents, or conversational interfaces

 - Experience with prompt engineering, model evals, or working with research teams on model behavior

 - Experience across consumer and enterprise products, including admin, permissions, privacy, and billing flows

 - Comfort working in code, such as editing strings, reviewing PRs, or prototyping with AI tools

 - Experience with localization and writing for global audiences


NOTES FOR CANDIDATES

We want to see portfolio work where your words changed the product. Show us the problem, the options you explored, the language you shipped, and what happened after. We value end-to-end ownership, range, and impact, and we'd love to see examples of AI-related work, such as prompts, evaluations, or content you designed for model output.

Perplexity is revolutionizing how companies get work done. We are seeking an Associate Product Marketing Manager to join our team and serve as the bridge between how our products actually work and how the world learns to use them. You will develop the deepest product understanding on the team and translate it into webinars and education materials that inspire adoption and drive growth.

If you have a passion for understanding how things work, thrive in taking something complex and making it simple, and want to build a world-class product education engine that turns new users into power users, this role is for you.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Know the product cold. Develop a deeper working knowledge of our products than anyone else in marketing, using every feature the day it ships, building the workflows yourself, and staying close to the teams that built them.

 - Turn complexity into clarity. Transform complex product capabilities into simple, specific, and accurate explanations, defining not just what we built, but how it works, when to use it, and why it matters.

 - Teach at scale. Own product webinars end to end, from content and live demos to delivery and follow-up, spanning onboarding series, feature deep-dives, and use-case walkthroughs.

 - Build the education engine. Create the product education materials our users learn from: how-to guides, demo flows, video walkthroughs, and use-case libraries that make customers materially better at their jobs.

 - Obsess over the user. Maintain a sharp, real-time view of what users misunderstand and where they get stuck, ensuring our education remains grounded in how people actually use the product rather than how we assume they do.

 - Measure outcomes, not just outputs. Tie webinars and education content to tangible activation, adoption, and retention, running lightweight experiments to iterate fast on format, content, and delivery.

 - Get products to launch. Own and coordinate the cross-functional workstreams that take products from built to launch, keeping teams aligned on dependencies, timelines, and the work needed to bring each launch to market.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 2-3 years of experience in product marketing, customer education, business development, or a related role, ideally within a high-growth technology company, or work that proves the skill regardless of title.

 - Proven ability to synthesize complex technical concepts into simple, specific, and provable explanations that travel across new users, power users, and admins.

 - Genuine obsession with product: you explore every setting, test every new feature, and can explain what a product does better than the team that built it.

 - Sharp teaching and storytelling skills grounded in data, with the ability to summarize how a feature works in a single sentence and demonstrate it live.

 - High slope: you learn unfamiliar products and domains fast, and your rate of improvement is your standout trait.

 - Extreme comfort delivering clarity in high-velocity, ambiguous environments.

Perplexity is looking for a commercially minded attorney to join our Legal team. In this role, you’ll own the full commercial legal lifecycle. You will draft, negotiate, and close a wide range of agreements across partnerships, procurement, infrastructure, and licensing. You will build scalable legal infrastructure and enable the business to move quickly without unacceptable risk.



You’ll work closely with teams across the business, including product, engineering, security, finance, and sales to close deals, strengthen our data security and compliance posture, and serve as a trusted advisor on the AI-specific legal questions that come with operating at the frontier of this technology. The ideal candidate brings deep experience negotiating a wide range of commercial technology agreements, including infrastructure and compute procurement agreements, a strong command of data privacy and security frameworks, and the practical judgment to make principled risk calls independently. This is a high-impact, hands-on role for someone who thrives in fast-paced environments, knows how to be a true partner to the business without being a bottleneck, and is excited to help build a best-in-class legal function at one of the most consequential AI companies in the world.



Responsibilities

 - Lead end-to-end drafting, review, and negotiation of commercial agreements, including MSAs, SaaS and API agreements, DPAs, partnership and reseller agreements, strategic collaboration and co-marketing agreements, procurement and vendor contracts, technology and infrastructure agreements, and IP licensing arrangements.

 - Serve as a primary legal partner across the business, providing fast, practical, and business-aligned counsel that accelerates deal velocity without compromising on risk Management.

 - Provide strategic counsel on legal risks across AI infrastructure, compute, partnerships, and enterprise deployments as the company scales.

 - Advise on AI-specific legal considerations in commercial agreements, including acceptable use, data retention and training restrictions, output liability, and evolving regulatory requirements (e.g., EU AI Act, CCPA/CPRA, GDPR).

 - Build and maintain scalable legal infrastructure—contract templates, negotiation playbooks, fallback positions, and tools (e.g., CLM, self-serve workflows)—to support high-volume deal flow and reduce friction in the contracting cycle.

 - Partner cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, Security, Finance, and Compliance teams to surface and address legal risk early, particularly on data use, enterprise integrations, and customer-specific compliance requirements.

 - Monitor the evolving regulatory landscape for enterprise AI and SaaS products and translate emerging requirements into practical contractual and policy guidance for internal stakeholders.

Qualifications

 - JD and in good standing with an active U.S. state bar membership.

 - At least 5+ years of law firm and/or in-house experience, with a track record of drafting and negotiating complex commercial technology agreements.

 - Strong business acumen and ability to partner effectively with sales, product, engineering, and executive teams.

 - Deep familiarity with data privacy and security frameworks (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, SOC 2, HIPAA) and experience negotiating DPAs and related compliance agreements.

 - Prior experience with infrastructure agreements is strongly preferred, including compute procurement (e.g., GPU capacity and cloud/neocloud agreements, colocation, and related SLA and acceptance terms).

 - Ability to communicate clearly with business and technical audiences and effectively translate legal concepts for non-lawyers.

 - Hands-on attitude to tackle projects large and small, low-ego approach to working across the organization.

 - Positive collaborative attitude, comfort with ambiguity and a fast pace, high level of integrity, and intellectual curiosity about AI technology and how these products work.

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.



Title and Pay dependent on YOE (Counsel or Senior Counsel)

Perplexity is looking for a technical program manager to be the connective tissue between our model providers, engineering, and product teams, driving our core inference platform forward.



Perplexity runs one of the highest-throughput inference stacks in the industry, serving Ask, Computer, and API traffic across a large and constantly shifting portfolio of first-party and third-party models. This role sits at the intersection of product, engineering, and finance: you'll orchestrate across model providers and internal teams to keep new models and capacity moving smoothly into production, while executing the roadmap for the inference platform itself. The ideal candidate has strong technical judgment, thrives coordinating across teams and external partners with competing timelines, and is energized by building the operating model for a function that doesn't have much precedent yet.




OUR MISSION

Perplexity's mission is to power curiosity. Curious people are the people who drive change in the world. Driving change is a continuous cycle of learning, building, and integrating.



Learn: curious people constantly learn new things by asking more. They question the status quo in their own expertise and they constantly learn outside of it. Research is essential to them and never ending.



Build: curious people make and create things, to show the world their new answers to problems no one else ever questioned. They take action on what they've learned. Makers need tools to create their products, their companies, their reality.



Integrate: they must interact with the world as it is to drive change and adoption. True leaders do not simply build something and hope. They must have armies of agents and workers who can constantly work in millions of small ways.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Execute the roadmap for the inference platform  request handling, rate limits and quotas, usage controls, and the reliability and observability surface engineering and product teams depend on

 - Be the connective tissue between model providers and Perplexity's engineering and product teams coordinating onboarding, launch readiness, and rollout for new models and capacity

 - Drive latency, throughput, uptime, and cost-efficiency as core execution metrics, surfacing tradeoffs between them rather than letting them become side effects

 - Run the operating model for model-release and optimization programs, including day-zero launches, across performance engineering, infrastructure, and product teams

 - Lead cross-functional delivery for inference-stack changes, from planning through launch and post-launch validation

 - Build the mechanisms that make releases predictable rituals, dashboards, launch checklists so inference releases stay low-risk at Perplexity's scale

 - Partner with GPU capacity and compute teams to reconcile execution decisions against cost, capacity, and vendor constraints




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Strong experience with technical program management or product management in infrastructure, distributed systems, or ML/model-serving products

 - Direct experience with production LLM or ML inference understanding what makes serving fast, reliable, and cheap rather than just what a roadmap slide says about it

 - Comfort orchestrating across external partners and internal engineering teams with competing priorities and timelines

 - Experience with data and metrics, and the judgment to surface difficult tradeoffs between latency, throughput, uptime, and cost

 - Thrives in a small, agile team; has initiative and desire for ownership without much precedent to lean on

 - 6+ years of combined technical program management or product management experience

job_title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, Cloud Infrastructure)
job_description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

The Cloud Infrastructure team owns the foundational cloud primitives and deployment models that power Perplexity's products, from multi-tenant public cloud to single-tenant and on-premises solutions for enterprise customers.

As Perplexity grows its Computer and Enterprise products, this team builds and operates the security, isolation, and compliance layers that customers depend on. We provide the deployment topologies, multi‑region infrastructure, and core services that enable Perplexity to run reliably and efficiently for both consumer traffic and large enterprises.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own the roadmap and technical strategy for agent-driven cloud infrastructure management.

 - Design and operate Perplexity’s cloud networking fabric, including VPC architectures, private connectivity, and peering with hyperscalers and neocloud providers to support low-latency, high-throughput AI workloads.

 - Architect and scale compute platforms (Kubernetes/EKS, autoscaling groups, and mixed CPU/GPU fleets) to efficiently serve online request traffic and background workloads across regions.

 - Build and maintain secure, isolated deployment topologies for multi-tenant, single-tenant, and customer‑owned cloud (BYOC) environments, including cross-account networking, identity, and policy guardrails.

 - Implement and evolve multi-region strategies for availability, failover, and data locality, including traffic routing, regional capacity planning, and disaster recovery playbooks.

 - Partner with security to deliver enterprise controls such as BYOK/KMS integrations, network isolation, and auditability required for regulated customers.

 - Develop automation, tooling, and runbooks that make day‑2 operations (provisioning, upgrades, incident response) predictable and repeatable for Perplexity products across all environments.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Deep experience designing and operating cloud infrastructure on AWS (VPC design, routing, security groups, load balancing, private connectivity).

 - Strong background with Kubernetes/EKS and container orchestration, including multi‑cluster, multi‑region, or multi‑account setups.

 - Hands-on experience with cloud networking and peering (VPC peering, Transit Gateway, private link/service endpoints, or similar constructs in neoclouds).

 - Experience building or operating secure, isolated environments for enterprise customers (single‑tenant, BYOC, or on‑prem), ideally including BYOK/KMS integrations and compliance constraints.

 - Proficiency with infrastructure as code (Terraform) and strong software engineering skills in at least one of Python, Go, or Rust for automation and tooling.

 - Strong debugging and incident management skills across distributed systems (networking, compute, and platform layers), with a track record of driving root‑cause analysis and long‑term fixes.

 - 7+ years of industry experience building and operating production cloud infrastructure, including leading the design of complex systems or migrations.



If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn’t match every qualification listed above.

job_title: Member of Technical Staff (Software Engineer, AI Policy and Strategic Initiatives)
job_description:

As a Member of Technical Staff in the Policy & Strategic Initiatives group, you'll occupy a front-row seat to the foremost policy issues animating the AI ecosystem. You'll also get a panoptic view of how leading AI companies operate, make decisions, and engage with broader society.

Those seeking to marry technical expertise and broader interests in law, policy, and corporate affairs will find a home in this role. You'll make contributions to Perplexity that defy traditional boundaries, with a bench of mentors who will push you to learn and grow day after day.

job_description:
Perplexity serves hundreds of millions of queries a month. Every answer, every Perplexity Computer task, and every enterprise deployment runs on production infrastructure owned by the Cloud Infrastructure team: a fleet of Kubernetes clusters across a multi-account AWS estate, private networks that reach hyperscalers and the neoclouds serving our models, and the storage underneath our user data and agentic workloads. We're looking for SREs who treat reliability as a software problem. You'll own compute, networking, and storage at scale and keep production stable while everything built on top of it is changing fast.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own production at scale. Run the compute, networking, and storage foundation behind Perplexity's consumer, Computer, API, and enterprise products, and own its availability, latency, and cost.

 - Run our Kubernetes fleet. Operate and upgrade the EKS clusters that host web services, search, datastores, and secure sandboxes. Tune scheduling, autoscaling, node lifecycle, DNS, and service networking so clusters stay healthy under bursty, fast-growing load.

 - Engineer the network. Design and operate VPC architectures, Transit Gateway and PrivateLink connectivity, load balancing, DNS, and egress across accounts, regions, and cloud providers.

 - Keep data durable and fast. Own the storage layer (EBS, S3, DynamoDB, and the managed databases and caches our services depend on), including performance, durability, backups, and restores that have actually been tested.

 - Manage everything as code. Run infrastructure through Terraform and CI/CD. Build reusable modules and guardrails, and make every change reviewable, repeatable, and safe to roll back.

 - Prepare for failures. Define SLOs, build alerts that someone can act on, design for zone and regional failure, and run game days and disaster-recovery exercises that prove recovery works.

 - Lead incident response. Be on the critical path when things break. Drive incidents to resolution, write blameless postmortems, and land the fixes so the same failure never pages anyone twice.

 - Scale ahead of demand. Own capacity planning, quotas, reservations, and cost efficiency so product launches and traffic spikes never wait on infrastructure.

 - Automate away the toil. Build tooling, increasingly agent-driven, that turns provisioning, upgrades, and remediation into self-serve, hands-off workflows for every engineering team.




QUALIFICATIONS

We expect you to have real depth in most of these:

 - Deep AWS expertise. You know VPC, IAM, EC2, EKS, ELB, Route 53, S3, EBS, etc. well past the console, including their limits, failure modes, and the bill that comes with them.

ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE WE VALUE

 - Enterprise and compliance environments: single-tenant or BYOC deployments, KMS/BYOK, SOC 2 or similar controls.

To do this, we are reimagining recommendation systems for the LLM era. Our goal is to combine the intelligence of frontier LLMs, the personalization context that comes from real product usage, and the continual learning capabilities of modern recommendation systems. We build systems that draw on past context and connected data sources to deeply understand each user's needs and recommend the actions that help them get the most out of Perplexity.




WHY PERPLEXITY IS DIFFERENT

 - Craftsmanship. We build high quality, tasteful products targeting both AI native and AI curious users.

 - Ownership. You identify the problem, design the solution and ship it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the personalization and ranking behind key product surfaces to make Perplexity more useful and drive impact on core user and business metrics.

 - Build user modeling that captures intent, preference, and propensity, and powers more relevant, more personalized experiences.

 - Design the decision layer that balances competing objectives to produce the best overall experience for the user.

 - Build the data and evaluation foundations that let these systems learn and improve with usage.

 - Help shape the technical direction of ranking, recommendations, and personalization at Perplexity.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Deep, hands-on experience building production recommendation, ranking, or personalization systems at scale.

 - Strong ML fundamentals, covering areas such as engagement modeling, model calibration, offline and online metrics, and online experimentation.

 - Experience integrating LLMs into ranking, retrieval, or personalization pipelines.

 - Taste and judgment for how personalization should work in an LLM-native product, and curiosity about reimagining it from first principles.

 - For tech leadership roles, we will also look for prior experience setting technical direction for recommendation/ranking projects.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with large-scale ranking and training infrastructure (multi-stage retrieval and ranking, feature stores, real-time serving).

 - Background in user understanding, feed ranking, notifications, growth, or lifecycle modeling.


OUR MISSION

Perplexity’s mission is to power curiosity. Curious people are the people who drive change in the world. Driving change is a continuous cycle of learning, building, and integrating.

Learn: curious people constantly learn new things by asking more. They question the status quo in their own expertise and they constantly learn outside of it. Research is essential to them and never ending.

Build: curious people make and create things, to show the world their new answers to problems no one else ever questioned. They take action on what they’ve learned. Makers need tools to create their products, their companies, their reality.

Repeat. For curious people this is a cycle that never ends.

We are looking for an AI Inference Engineer to join our growing team. We build and run the inference engine behind every Perplexity query and deploy dozens of model architectures at scale with tight latency and cost budgets. Our stack is Rust, Python, CUDA, and CuTe DSL.





RESPONSIBILITIES: 

 - New models support. Support transformer-based retrieval, text-generation, and multimodal models in our inference infrastructure, from weight loading, request scheduling and KV-cache management to support in API Gateway.

 - GPU kernels migration to CuTe DSL. Port our in-house CUDA kernels to NVIDIA's CuTe DSL so they run on GB200 today and are portable to Vera Rubin racks tomorrow.

 - Rust-native serving runtime. Develop our internal Rust-based inference server to solve all Python pains and keep up with rapidly growing traffic.

 - Performance optimisation. Profile and fix bottlenecks from network ingress through continuous batching and GPU kernels interleaving.

 - Reliability and observability. Build dashboards, alerts, and automated remediation so we catch regressions before users do. Respond to and learn from production incidents.


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR:

 - Deep experience with GPU programming and performance work (CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS, or similar). Any other deep systems programming experience is a plus.

 - You understand modern LLM architectures and are able to bring them up reliably in a production environment.

 - You've built and operated production distributed systems under real load - ideally performance-critical ones.

 - Comfortable working across languages and layers: Rust for the serving runtime, Python for model code, CUDA/CuteDSL for kernels.

 - You own problems end-to-end. You can read a research paper on Monday, write a kernel on Wednesday, and debug a production incident on Friday.

 - Self-directed. You do well in fast-moving environments where the path forward isn't laid out for you.


NICE-TO-HAVE: 

 - ML compilers and framework internals: PyTorch internals, torch.compile, custom operators.

 - Distributed GPU communication: NCCL, NVLink, InfiniBand, RDMA libraries, model/tensor parallelism.

 - Low-precision inference: INT8/FP8/FP4 quantization, mixed-precision serving.

 - Profiling and debugging tools: Nsight Compute/Systems, CUDA-GDB, PTX/SASS analysis.

 - Container orchestration: Kubernetes, GPU scheduling, autoscaling inference workloads.


QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 3+ years of professional software engineering experience with meaningful work on ML inference or high-performance systems.

 - Familiarity with at least one deep learning framework (PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow).

 - Understanding of GPU architectures (memory hierarchy, warp scheduling, tensor cores).

 - Understanding of common LLM architectures and inference optimization techniques (e.g. quantization, speculative decoding, prefill-decode disaggregation).
